newsitem.title: CHINA: Jiang Zemin's protege elected Beijing mayor.
newsitem.headline: Jiang Zemin's protege elected Beijing mayor.

text.p: Jia Qinglin was formally elected mayor of Beijing on Saturday and pledged allegiance to his mentor, China's Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin, the Xinhua news agency said.

"We must be under the firm leadership of the Communist Party Central Committee with Jiang Zemin at the core," said Jia, who was already acting mayor and the capital's Communist Party deputy secretary.
The Beijing People's Congress elected the 57-year-old Jia as mayor to replace Li Qiyan, who has been appointed vice-minister of labour.
Li was a protege of Chen Xitong, who resigned as Beijing's Communist Party boss in April 1995 after a vice-mayor committed suicide after coming under investigation for corruption.
The new mayor said he would work closely with the Communist Party Central Committee and that his first priority was to safeguard the stability of Beijing.
He also vowed to further build a clean government and maintain close contacts with the public, Xinhua said.
